relevance_reason: The paper is relevant to KIF1B-related CMT2A1. A safety check blocked the earlier extraction attempt, so no findings are included here; this paper needs to be curated by hand.
Reports a loss-of-function mutation in the KIF1B motor domain in CMT2A patients, along with a knockout mouse model that supports it.

findings.statement: Zhao et al. (2001) found a loss-of-function mutation in the motor domain of the KIF1B gene in patients with CMT2A, a disorder previously mapped to an interval that contains KIF1B. They concluded that defects in axonal transport caused by a mutated motor protein can underlie human peripheral neuropathy.
quotes: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2A was previously mapped to an interval containing KIF1B.
We show that CMT2A patients contain a loss-of-function mutation in the motor domain of the KIF1B gene.
This is clear indication that defects in axonal transport due to a mutated motor protein can underlie human peripheral neuropathy.

findings.statement: Zhao et al. (2001) reported that Kif1b knockout mice died at birth from apnea caused by nervous system defects, and that knockout neurons dying in culture could be rescued by expressing the KIF1B-beta isoform. Heterozygous mice had a defect in transporting synaptic vesicle precursors and developed progressive muscle weakness similar to human neuropathies.
quotes: KIF1B knockout mice die at birth from apnea due to nervous system defects.
Death of knockout neurons in culture can be rescued by expression of the beta isoform.
The KIF1B heterozygotes have a defect in transporting synaptic vesicle precursors and suffer from progressive muscle weakness similar to human neuropathies.

findings.statement: Zhao et al. (2001) described KIF1B-beta, an isoform of the kinesin superfamily motor protein KIF1B that differs from KIF1B in its cargo-binding domain. KIF1B had previously been shown to transport mitochondria.
quotes: The kinesin superfamily motor protein KIF1B has been shown to transport mitochondria.
Here, we describe an isoform of KIF1B, KIF1Bbeta, that is distinct from KIF1B in its cargo binding domain.

relevance_reason: Linkage of CMT2 in two Japanese families to the CMT2A locus on 1p, with a description of the clinical features of CMT2A.

findings.statement: Saito et al. (1997) performed linkage analysis in 2 Japanese families with CMT2 and obtained a highest cumulative multipoint lod score of 3.69 at marker D1S244, consistent with linkage to the CMT2A locus on chromosome 1p35-p36.
quotes: we performed linkage analysis of two Japanese CMT2 families using markers flanking the CMT2A, CMT2B, and CMT2D loci. The highest cumulative multipoint lod score of 3.69 was obtained at D1S244.

findings.statement: Saito et al. (1997) excluded the CMT2B and CMT2D loci in the 2 Japanese CMT2 families by linkage analysis with markers D3S1551, D3S1290, and D7S484.
quotes: The CMT2B and CMT2D loci were excluded by the results of linkage analysis performed using markers D3S1551, D3S1290, and D7S484.

findings.statement: Saito et al. (1997) described the clinical features of CMT2A in 2 Japanese families. The posterior and anterior tibial muscles were similarly weak. Tendon reflexes were preserved in the upper limbs but reduced or absent in the lower limbs. The peripheral nerves were not enlarged, and only 20% of affected individuals had mild sensory disturbance.
quotes: The clinical features of the CMT2A affecting the two families include similar levels of muscle weakness of the posterior and anterior tibial muscles, tendon reflexes preserved in upper extremities but reduced or absent in lower extremities, no enlargement of the peripheral nerves, and mild sensory disturbance in only 20% of affected individuals.

phenotypes.text: weakness of posterior and anterior tibial muscles
reduced or absent tendon reflexes in lower extremities
tendon reflexes preserved in upper extremities

relevance_reason: Original linkage study that mapped the CMT2A locus to distal chromosome 1p and showed CMT2 is genetically heterogeneous.

findings.statement: Ben Othmane et al. (1993) performed pedigree linkage analysis in 6 large autosomal dominant CMT2 families and demonstrated linkage to microsatellite markers D1S160, D1S170, D1S244, D1S228, and D1S199 in the distal region of the short arm of chromosome 1. Multipoint analysis of the linked families placed the CMT2A gene most likely within the interval flanked by D1S244 and D1S228, with odds of approximately 70:1 for lying within versus outside that interval.
quotes: We have performed pedigree linkage analysis in six large autosomal dominant CMT2 families and have demonstrated linkage and heterogeneity to a series of microsatellites (D1S160, D1S170, D1S244, D1S228 and D1S199) in the distal region of the short arm of chromosome 1.

Multipoint analysis examining the "linked" families showed that the most favored location for the CMT2A gene is within the interval flanked by D1S244 and D1S228 (odds approximately 70:1 of lying within versus outside that interval).

findings.statement: Ben Othmane et al. (1993) found significant evidence for genetic heterogeneity among 6 CMT2 families using admixture analysis of two-point lod scores, supported by multipoint admixture analysis. Three families (DUK662, DUK1241, and 1523) had posterior probabilities of 1.0, 0.98, and 0.88 of being of the linked type. The authors suggested that the CMT2 phenotype results from at least 2 different genes.
quotes: Significant evidence for heterogeneity was found using admixture analysis and the two-point lod scores.
Three families, DUK662, DUK1241, and 1523 gave posterior probabilities of 1.0, 0.98, and 0.88 of being of the linked type.
These findings suggest that the CMT2 phenotype is secondary to at least two different genes and demonstrate further heterogeneity in the CMT phenotype.

findings.statement: Ben Othmane et al. (1993) described CMT2 as an inherited peripheral neuropathy with variable age of onset and normal or slightly reduced nerve conduction velocity, distinct pathologically and genetically from CMT1.
quotes: Charcot-Marie-Tooth (CMT) disease type 2 (CMT2) is an inherited peripheral neuropathy characterized by variable age of onset and normal or slightly diminished nerve conduction velocity. CMT2 is pathologically and genetically distinct from CMT type 1 (CMT1).

phenotypes.text: normal or slightly diminished nerve conduction velocity

relevance_reason: Linkage exclusion study showing that CMT2 is genetically distinct from the CMT1A and CMT1B loci, which is evidence for heterogeneity relevant to the CMT2 entry.

findings.statement: Hentati et al. (1992) studied 2 CMT2 pedigrees and excluded the CMT2 locus from the chromosome 17 region where CMT1A maps (lod score -2.80 at theta = 0.05 for D17S58). In a CMT1 pedigree studied alongside them, CMT1A linkage was confirmed (lod +3.67 at theta = 0.00). Negative lod scores were also obtained in CMT2 for the chromosome 1 region containing CMT1B (lod -3.09 at theta = 0.05 for D1S61).
quotes: Studying one CMT1 and two CMT2 pedigrees, we were able to exclude the CMT2 disease locus from the region of chromosome 17 (Z = -2.80 at theta = 0.05 for D17S58) where the CMT1A gene maps (Z = +3.67 at theta = 0.00).
Similarly, negative lod score values were obtained in CMT2 for the region of chromosome 1 where the CMT1B gene has been located (Z = -3.09 at theta = 0.05 for D1S61).

findings.statement: Hentati et al. (1992) concluded that the hypertrophic (CMT1) and neuronal (CMT2) forms of Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease are genetically heterogeneous. They found that the CMT2 gene is not allelic to either of the CMT1 genes mapped at that time.
quotes: The present study therefore provides evidence for genetic heterogeneity between the hypertrophic and the neuronal forms of Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease and demonstrates that the CMT2 gene is not allelic to either of the CMT1 genes mapped to date.
